newsitem.title: INDONESIA: US, Italian firms sign Indonesia power supply deal.
newsitem.headline: US, Italian firms sign Indonesia power supply deal.

text.p: A joint venture between Italy's Ansaldo Energia S.p.A and NRG Energy Inc of the United States signed an agreement on Wednesday to sell power to Indonesia's state electricity firm PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN).
"Under the agreement PLN will buy electricity at 6.06 U.S. cents per kilowatt hour," PLN said in statement.
A PLN official said the agreement will run for 30 years.
The electricity will come from a 400 megawatt power plant to be built by the joint venture PT Daya Listrik Pratama at a cost of around $564 million in West Java.
Ansaldo and NRG Energy have a 45 percent stake each in Daya. The rest is owned by local company PT Fenergi Cipta.
"I hope that with the signing of this power purchase agreement, the power plant can be operational by 1999," Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said after the signing.
